questions: Should the function raise an error or return something specific (e.g., empty list, NaN) if the input array is empty?
Is the threshold inclusive or exclusive (i.e., > threshold vs. >= threshold)?
Should the variance be population variance (N) or sample variance (N-1)?
If standard deviation is 0, should the mean and variance still be returned as computed (e.g., mean of data, variance 0)?
Are indices returned as Python ints or numpy integers?
Should the function handle non-finite values (NaN, inf) in the input array?
Is the distribution fitted always a normal distribution, or could it be another distribution based on data?
Should the mean and variance be computed from the fitted distribution (norm.fit) or directly from data (np.mean, np.var)?
